video.title: Don’t Sleep on This Specific $0-to-Millions Reselling Strategy

summary: Host Chris Koerner interviews reseller and liquidator Shannon about buying discounted liquidation lots and finding buyers before bidding. Shannon describes his past handbag business, examples involving industrial goods, apparel and other categories, and the research and sales processes he uses. His central advice is to build a repeatable system, check what inventory can sell for before buying it, and make sure the deal leaves room for freight and resale work. The examples are hands-on, but the businesses depend on sourcing, handling and shipping physical inventory.

speakers.name: Shannon
speakers.description: Reseller, flipper and liquidator; no surname is stated.

ideas.name: Liquidation lot resale
ideas.one_liner: Buy discounted pallets or truckloads, research their resale value, and sell the goods individually or in bulk.
ideas.business_model: Buy inventory below resale value and resell it through marketplaces or directly to buyers.
ideas.customer: Consumers, retailers, tradespeople and other businesses that need the goods in a liquidation lot.
ideas.problem: Buyers want goods below retail prices; liquidators need to move surplus or returned stock.
ideas.offer: Resell liquidation goods at a discount to their stated store price.

pricing.model: Buy lots at a fraction of stated retail value and resell individual items or groups.

price_points.unit: cents per $1 of stated retail value
price_points.label: Guest's description of lot acquisition prices

price_points.unit: cents per $1 of stated retail value
price_points.label: Host's description of resale prices

pricing.notes: The host gives the 2–5 and 20–30 cent figures while introducing Shannon; treat them as the host's summary.

acquisition_channels.details: Shannon buys liquidation lots through B-Stock and Costco's liquidation auctions; he recommends researching lots before bidding.

quote.text: I've bought a lot of stuff from Costco over the years from their auction, the liquidation site, and you get loads of that
quote.speaker: Shannon

acquisition_channels.details: He posts auction examples and deals on X and in his mastermind; posts can also connect him with people who know a product market.

quote.text: I posted about it. It's at the Signature Hardware link and I posted a link. I'm here, go buy this.
quote.speaker: Shannon

acquisition_channels.details: He calls likely buyers to learn whether they want the goods and what they would pay. In the UK, screen calls against TPS or CTPS as applicable.

quote.text: But the one thing people don't do is nobody likes to pick up the phone, right?
quote.speaker: Shannon

acquisition_channels.details: He uses LinkedIn to find platform category managers and suppliers, build familiarity and make himself known before asking to speak or collaborate.

quote.text: I find the product managers and the category managers and I reach out.
quote.speaker: Shannon

ideas.delivery: Acquire physical lots, sort and prepare the goods, then sell through online marketplaces or to business buyers. Shannon describes personally researching and selling; his wife has shipped some inventory. Freight, storage, listing and fulfilment work vary by lot.
unit_economics_claims: The host says Shannon buys at 2–5 cents on the dollar and resells at 20–30 cents on the dollar.
Shannon says to discount stated store prices when estimating resale value and include shipping in landed cost.
A product equation or spreadsheet is used to compare a bid with possible resale proceeds.
ideas.startup_cost: $0 starting capital is claimed as possible if the deal is good enough to secure financing; actual lot and freight costs vary.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; Shannon says to research before buying and not rush into a lot.

acquisition.how: Agents could monitor auction listings and estimate resale values, but bidding, supplier checks and buyer calls need human oversight. UK marketing automation must respect PECR and call-screening rules.

onboarding.how: Auction registration and resale-permit requirements are not described as automated; lot manifests and shipping terms need human review.

delivery.how: Physical goods must be received, checked, stored, packaged and shipped. Software can assist with labels and inventory records.

billing.how: Marketplace checkout can handle routine payment, while direct business orders, freight charges and refunds need review.

support.how: Agents could answer routine order questions, but returns, damaged goods and disputes need human judgment.

uk_applicability.notes: The buy-low, resell approach can work in the UK, but auction access, resale permissions, VAT, freight and marketplace rules may differ. Use lawful inbound marketing and screened calls.

risks: A manifest or item condition can be misunderstood, leaving unsellable or hard-to-sell stock.
Freight, storage, returns and labour can erase the apparent discount.
Inventory is not passive income; Shannon says it takes work and consistency.
Cold electronic messages to UK individuals and sole traders require consent under PECR; screen cold calls against TPS or CTPS as applicable.

ideas.name: Luxury handbag resale
ideas.one_liner: Learn the luxury handbag market, source bags and resell them on fashion marketplaces with strong service and presentation.
ideas.business_model: Buy handbags for resale through marketplaces.
ideas.problem: Buyers want luxury bags but may distrust online sellers and worry about authenticity, condition and delivery.
ideas.offer: Luxury handbags supported by authenticity guarantees, careful packaging, free returns and attentive customer service.

pricing.model: Per-item resale; exact sale prices are not stated.
pricing.notes: Shannon describes first planning to sell multiple lower-priced bags, then moving up to higher-value bags.

acquisition_channels.details: He sold most items on Poshmark and eBay and researched other options including Mercari and Whatnot.

quote.text: I've sold most of the stuff on Poshmark and eBay.
quote.speaker: Shannon

acquisition_channels.details: He contacted platform category managers and built relationships before he needed help with his accounts.

quote.text: I go on LinkedIn, I'd find what they were doing and I'd be like, Man, I'm having such a great time.
quote.speaker: Shannon

ideas.delivery: Source and list bags on marketplaces, photograph them, guarantee authenticity, package them carefully and ship them. Shannon says his wife shipped some items and he offered free returns.
unit_economics_claims: Shannon says he sold about $4 million worth of handbags over three years and made $557,000 net profit.
He describes a target of $500 per day, first by selling ten bags for $50 each, then by moving up to one higher-value bag per day.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Shannon says it took 8–12 months before the business gained traction.

acquisition.how: Agents can draft marketplace listings and monitor demand, but sourcing and trust-building with platform staff require human judgment. Avoid unsolicited UK DMs or messages.

onboarding.how: Listing forms and buyer messages can be templated, but authentication, condition grading and item photography need checks.

delivery.how: An agent can prepare labels and packing instructions, but a person must inspect, package and ship each bag.

billing.how: Marketplace payment systems can handle routine checkout; refunds and return decisions need oversight.

support.how: Agents could handle standard order updates, but authenticity or condition complaints call for empathetic human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Luxury resale can translate to the UK, but platform mix, authentication expectations, consumer returns, VAT and sourcing differ. UK buyers and sellers need clear evidence of authenticity.

risks: Counterfeit or misdescribed goods can lead to disputes and marketplace penalties.
Marketplace account limits or suspensions can interrupt sales; Shannon advises building platform relationships in advance.
Returns and careful packaging reduce margin and require physical handling.
The guest says live selling is an important sales format for handbags, which may require a capable on-camera seller.

tactics.name: Validate buyers before bidding
steps: Find the likely resale market for a product before bidding.
Use eBay Product Research to check sold prices and the number of sales.
Call likely business buyers to ask what they need and what price they would pay.
Only bid once you have a credible route to recovering the purchase cost.

quote.text: the first law of auctions is never buy anything unless you know what you can already sell it for.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Calculate a conservative landed bid
steps: Discount the stated retail price because Shannon says it can be misleading.
Estimate a cautious resale value and subtract freight and other costs.
Use a spreadsheet or product equation to set a maximum bid.
Bid with math rather than emotion.

quote.text: I use math to bid, not emotion. I've studied. I've done my research.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Study a category before scaling
steps: Watch auctions and research the category before making large purchases.
Make small mistakes while the stakes are low.
Learn how listings, photos, authenticity, shipping and returns work.
Move into larger lots only after the market and process make sense.

quote.text: So studying that when you can make small mistakes is really powerful and that's what I was doing.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Build platform relationships before problems arise
steps: Find platform category managers and product managers on LinkedIn.
Interact with their public posts and congratulate them on relevant work.
Send a short introduction explaining the category and sales activity.
Offer to speak about the seller experience, then build the relationship over time.

quote.text: You don't want to ask him for anything, but you want to get in his conversation flow.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Differentiate listings with evidence
steps: Look at what other sellers include in their listings.
For used goods, record a short video showing the item working.
Use clear photography and explain condition accurately.
For high-value goods, package them carefully and include a thank-you card or coupon where economics allow.

quote.text: I've got video of me walking around or if it's used I have a video of it working all that kind of stuff.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Handle complaints with empathy
steps: Acknowledge the customer's disappointment instead of arguing about fault.
Offer a prepaid return label promptly.
Consider a future-purchase coupon when it is economically sensible.
Take responsibility for the overall transaction and delivery experience.

quote.text: So, you always choose the end of the world token and you say, Oh my gosh, I'm so sorry.
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Sell bulk goods to the businesses that use them
steps: Identify businesses that consume or transform the product, such as screen printers for blank apparel.
Use the lot manifest to explain what is available.
Ask potential buyers what they would pay before buying the inventory.
Follow up when a suitable lot becomes available.

quote.text: The story just tell them the truth. Hey, I'm I'm in the resale business and I get all these opportunities
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Look for an unfair advantage
steps: Identify what you can do better than other sellers: capital, storage, delivery, expertise or customer service.
Choose product categories where that advantage matters.
Use the advantage to make an otherwise difficult lot easier to buy or sell.

quote.text: I call it what is your unfair advantage? What do you have that other people don't?
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Track product and category changes
steps: Watch how product design and repairability change over time.
Notice when a previously profitable category loses parts or margin.
Move research to another category rather than assuming the old opportunity will persist.

quote.text: Nothing stays the same. And if and if you don't continually invol evolve what you're working on, you'll be left behind.
quote.speaker: Shannon

quote.speaker: Shannon

lessons.lesson: Make sure there is a realistic path to recovering your investment before treating remaining inventory as upside.

quote.text: what do I have to do just to get my money back? That's all I'm thinking about

evidence_quality.rationale: Shannon describes first-hand businesses, detailed sourcing and sales processes, and specific results. Some examples are from other resellers or hypothetical calculations, and several figures are difficult to verify from the conversation alone.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host mentions Shannon's $5-per-month mastermind and says he receives nothing from it or the auction companies; the mastermind is a promotional conflict to note.
